newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA OLD MUTUAL SEES SMALL CAP STOCK DEMAND UP.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA OLD MUTUAL SEES SMALL CAP STOCK DEMAND UP.

text.p: South Africa's biggest insurer Old Mutual said on Thursday it saw continued strong growth in small stocks on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) over the next two years as demand was already outstripping supply.
The firm said heavy demand for smaller capitalisation shares helped Old Mutual Unit Trusts's Small Companies Fund to breach the 200 million rand mark in its first three months.

"Investors who backed the new fund have been rewarded with a 40 percent return since inception and, given a strong stock market, there clearly seems scope for more," Old Mutual head of research Bryan Hopkins told the media on Thursday.
While Old Mutual Unit Trusts attracted some three million rand a day, Hopkins estimated that about 1.9 billion rand flowed into small company unit trusts in the second quarter of this year.
"We believe this is only the start as more investors become aware of the profit potential," he said.
Hopkins said he aimed to achieve a 30 percent return a year and, despite the current high prices of many of the small favourites, believed that the sector's re-rating had only begun.

"We would hope that our top five holdings will be able to achieve on average a 40 percent growth over the next 12 months and profitability may be even higher if interest rates are cut this year," said joint portfolio manager Brendan Burgess.
Small company shares favoured by Old Mutual include Invicta Holdings Ltd, Capital Alliance Holdings Ltd and Nu World Holdings Ltd.
Hopkins said the continued re-rating of small stocks was bound to lead to more new listings on the JSE.
